h1: Ban's Diving Resort — A Dive Resort on Sairee Beach in the Heart of Koh Tao, with an In-House Dive School
intro: When it comes to Koh Tao, the island that certifies more new divers than anywhere else in the world · Ban's Diving Resort is a name almost everyone has heard — a large PADI 5-Star dive resort that has been going since 1993, set right on Sairee Beach, the island's busiest main beach, packed with restaurants, bars, and dive centres · the place is like a little village of its own, with 4 swimming pools, a beachfront restaurant, a sunset-view bar, and an in-house dive centre · rooms run from budget fan bungalows all the way to air-con pool-view rooms, from approx. ฿700/night · 8.0 from real guest reviews.

body.html: First, the thing you need to know — Koh Tao has no airport. The way to get here is to take a high-speed catamaran such as Lomprayah or Songserm from Chumphon (the fastest, ~1.5–2 hrs), from Surat Thani, Koh Samui, or Koh Phangan, arriving at Mae Haad pier, the island's main pier and village · from Mae Haad it's just another 5–10 minutes by songthaew/taxi into Sairee Beach, and Ban's is right there · worth knowing: during the late-year monsoon (roughly October–December) the sea can get rough and boats may pitch about or be cancelled altogether, so build in extra time and always check the weather before booking your tickets.

Location is the main selling point here · Sairee is the longest and liveliest beach on Koh Tao — unlike Chalok Baan Kao to the south, which is quieter, or Tanote Bay and Haad Tien/Shark Bay, which are secluded, private corners further out · Sairee is the side that has everything within walking distance: restaurants, cafés, bars, convenience stores, and dive centres lined up all along the beach · Ban's sits right in the middle of this beach, and many guests say the big advantage is being able to walk out for a meal, a drink, or a dive boat without ever calling for a ride.

As the name says, Ban's is a full-on dive resort — a PADI 5-Star Career & Instructor Development Centre that has long been called the centre that certifies more divers than any other in the world · this is the charm of Koh Tao, where many places to stay are dive resorts where you can learn to dive on site: book an Open Water or Advanced course and stay in one place from start to finish · people who come to learn often get a good room+course deal, and reviews frequently praise the teaching quality and the value of the courses · if you're set on getting certified, this is one of the first names people think of.

"Came for a four-day Open Water course and still didn't want to leave when it was done — dive boat in the morning, pool in the afternoon, then the beach bar for sunset in the evening. Everything's in one place."

The resort itself is bigger than you'd expect, like a little village spread out in the middle of Sairee Beach · there are 4 swimming pools, a leafy garden, a gym, a spa and hair salon, a dive centre, a conservation centre, two 24-hour minimarts, and an in-house ATM · on the food and drink side there's a beachfront restaurant, Darawan, the Coffee House & Pool Bar, and the Fish Bowl bar, a hugely popular sunset-watching spot with live music almost every night · the facilities are complete enough that some guests barely need to leave.

The rooms come in a wide range to suit every budget · at the budget end are the fan bungalows in the garden/on the hillside, from around ฿750, ideal for backpacker divers who spend the whole day out on the water anyway · a step up gets you an air-con Superior room with a garden/pool view at around ฿1,400, and a Deluxe pool-view room with a balcony at around ฿2,300 · and for those who want the largest space there are suites/pool-access rooms at around ฿3,800 · a straight observation from the reviews: room quality is inconsistent, the cheap fan rooms are fairly basic and dated, and some rooms are up a steep hill that takes a fair walk — if you don't want a long climb, ask for a lower-zone room when you book.

The things that have to be said in fairness — the Booking.com score sits at 7.6/10, which isn't sky-high · the recurring complaints are the hot water not always coming through (cold showers), cleanliness and pool upkeep at times, and noise at night · another point that surprises many is that the resort is split in two by a road with no dedicated crossing, so you have to wait for traffic and cross to the reception, breakfast, and beach side · and because it's big and busy, at peak season it can feel like a diver-production factory, hectic, with noise from the beach bar late into the night.

So what about the service? · the point reviews agree on most is that the staff are friendly and helpful, especially the dive team and the front desk · and while the Booking score is middling, on TripAdvisor, which measures the long-term overall picture, Ban's is ranked #1 of 52 hotels on Koh Tao, with 4.6/5 from over 6,700 reviews, and Trip.com gives it 8.5/10 · the gap between the scores captures what this place is really about — if you're here for the diving, the location, and the sociable beach vibe, you'll love it, but if you're expecting immaculate, quiet, luxury-resort rooms, you may need to adjust your expectations.
"The fan room was a touch basic and the hot water came and went, but the location in the middle of Sairee makes everything an easy walk, and the staff are so lovely — well worth what you pay."

The friend-to-friend summary · Ban's Diving Resort is best for people coming to Koh Tao to dive who want to be in the thick of the Sairee Beach buzz · you get an in-house dive centre, 4 pools, a beachfront restaurant and bar, and a location within walking distance of everything, at flexible prices from a few hundred baht to a few thousand · but you have to make peace with basic fan rooms, cold showers, a hill to climb, a road cutting through the middle, and the crowds at peak times · if you can live with those trade-offs in return for the location and the dive deals, this is one of the island's most-repeated stays.

A tip from reading the real reviews: if you're not a hardcore backpacker, spend the extra to get an air-con pool-view room — it's a lot more comfortable than the fan rooms both in temperature and in how fresh it feels · ask for a lower-zone room if you don't want the hill climb · if you're a light sleeper, request a room away from the beach bar · and if you're here to learn to dive, ask about a combined course + accommodation package, which usually works out cheaper than booking them separately.

honestSummary: Ban's Diving Resort is a dive resort that's best for people coming to Koh Tao to dive who want to be in the thick of the Sairee Beach buzz — an in-house PADI 5-Star centre, 4 pools, a beachfront restaurant and bar, and a location within walking distance of everything, at flexible prices from a few hundred baht · just make peace with basic fan rooms, cold showers, a hill to climb, a road through the middle, and the crowds at peak times.
honestChecks: If you want immaculate, quiet, luxury-resort rooms — this is a large, busy dive resort with basic entry-level rooms → upgrade to an air-con pool-view room, or choose a quieter bay-side stay like Chalok or Haad Tien instead.
If you can't manage a hill climb or dread cold showers — some rooms are up a steep hill and the fan rooms' hot water is unreliable → ask for a lower-zone air-con room when you book.
If you're a light sleeper who worries about noise — the Sairee beach bars have live music late into the night → request a room away from the beach and the bars.

faqTitle: Frequently asked questions — Ban's Diving Resort, Koh Tao

faq.q: Where is Ban's Diving Resort on Koh Tao, and how do you get there?
faq.a: It's right on Sairee Beach in the heart of Koh Tao, the busiest main beach, a walk from restaurants, bars, and dive centres · getting there: take a high-speed Lomprayah or Songserm catamaran from Chumphon (~1.5–2 hrs), Surat Thani, Koh Samui, or Koh Phangan to Mae Haad pier, then a songthaew/taxi into Sairee, another ~5–10 min · during the late-year monsoon the sea can be rough and boats may be cancelled, so check the weather first.

faq.q: How much does Ban's Diving Resort cost, and what room types are there?
faq.a: Prices start from approx. ฿700–฿750/night for a fan bungalow · a Superior air-con room with a garden/pool view starts around ฿1,400 · a Deluxe pool-view room with a balcony around ฿2,300 · a suite/pool-access room around ฿3,800 · prices depend on the season and there may be deals that bundle in a dive course, so always compare a few platforms before booking (prices approximate).

faq.q: Can you learn to dive at Ban's Diving Resort?
faq.a: Yes · this is a PADI 5-Star Career & Instructor Development Centre that has been running since 1993 and is called the centre that certifies more divers than any other in the world · you can do Open Water, Advanced, and right up to instructor-level courses on site, and there are often combined course + accommodation packages that are better value than booking separately.

faq.q: Who is Ban's Diving Resort best for?
faq.a: It's a great fit for divers and people who want to be in the thick of the Sairee Beach buzz · you get an in-house dive centre, 4 pools, a beachfront restaurant and bar, and a location within walking distance of everything, at flexible prices from a few hundred baht · but if you want a quiet, private atmosphere or luxury-resort-level rooms, a stay over on the Chalok Baan Kao or Haad Tien side may suit you more.

faq.q: What should you know about the downsides of Ban's Diving Resort?
faq.a: From the real reviews: the resort is split by a road with no dedicated crossing, so you wait for traffic and cross to the beach side · room quality is inconsistent, the cheap fan rooms are basic and some are up a steep hill · there are complaints about cold showers, pool upkeep at times, and noise from the beach bar late at night · the Booking.com score is 7.6/10, but TripAdvisor ranks it #1 of 52 hotels on the island (4.6/5).

faq.q: How far in advance should you book?
faq.a: For high season (December–April) and festival periods, book 3–4 weeks or more ahead, as Koh Tao gets busy and air-con pool-view rooms sell out fast · otherwise 1–2 weeks is fine · in the late-year monsoon, have a backup plan for the boats too · pick Free Cancellation first if your plans aren't firm, then compare prices for the same room type across a few sites.
